worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 50,000.00 + long-term gains 2,500.00 = 52,500.00. Federal taxable income = 52,500.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 36,750.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, single. Line 9 federal AGI 52,500.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 15,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 52,500.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 36,667.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 16 net capital gains: smaller of 2,500.00 and the cap 2,500.00 = 2,500.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 2,500.00. Line 17 = 52,500.00 + 0.00 - 15,750.00 - 0.00 - 2,500.00 = 34,250.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 36,750.00 - 2,500.00 = 34,250.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 34,250.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 5,500.00 = 82.5 + 3.2% x 11,000.00 = 352 + 4.3% x 17,000.00 = 731 + 4.7% x 750.00 = 35.25; total 1,200.75, to the cent 1,200.75. The table row over 34,200 to 34,300 gives 1,201; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 1,200.75.
